literal: Than the face, that which is wise is there? Even if pleased, even if angry, it will precede.
translation: Is there anything more perceptive than the face? Whether the mind feels joy or anger, the face shows it first.
modern: ஒருவர் மகிழ்ந்தாலும் கோபப்பட்டாலும், அதை அவருக்கு முன்பாகவே அவரது முகம் காட்டிவிடும். எனவே முகத்தை விட அறிவுடையது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the face as the ultimate mirror of the mind. The word 'mutukkuṟaintatu' refers to mature wisdom or sharp intelligence, attributing a perceptive quality to the face. Because the face instantly reveals inner feelings like joy or anger before the person even speaks, it is considered the most intelligent part of the body.
